title: The Evening Brief: Saturday's tape shows whales moving onto exchanges as markets hold steady
dek: No published stories arrived Saturday, but the desk's boards show a quiet day in price action offset by significant whale accumulation onto exchanges, notably $1.5 billion in the week ending today.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: The week ending October 10 saw whales move $1.5 billion net onto exchanges, the largest weekly accumulation in recent weeks, while retail ETF positions show divergent signals: bitcoin ETF inflows on the day but ethereum ETF outflows for nine consecutive sessions.
bottom_line: Saturday was data-driven, with no new stories to move sentiment: price action stayed range-bound across the day, but whale flows across the week ending today reached $1.5 billion net onto exchanges, the most in recent weeks per the desk's Whale Watch board. Bitcoin ETF flows turned positive on the day but remain outflows over five sessions; ethereum ETF flows extended a nine-day losing streak.
body: Saturday brought no new desk reporting, leaving the market picture to the data. The fear and greed index stands at 64 in the greed zone, with the 30-day range between 50 and 78.

Whale flows told a larger story. The desk's Whale Watch board shows $109.6 million net moving onto exchanges over the past 24 hours, with bitcoin accounting for $57.9 million and Solana for $51.6 million onto Binance and Coinbase Institutional respectively. Over the week ending October 10, the pattern intensified: $1.5 billion net moved onto exchanges, the highest weekly figure in at least three weeks. Earlier weeks ending September 19, September 26, and October 3 each saw between $428 million and $804 million move onto exchanges. This sustained pattern suggests either accumulation or preparation for position adjustment.
ETF flows remained mixed. Cumulative year-to-date flows for bitcoin stand at $57.2 billion and ethereum at $13.3 billion.

Leverage and liquidations showed mixed positioning. Bitcoin funding rates on OKX sat at negative 0.0031 percent per 8 hours (negative 3.4 percent annualized), with a long-to-short ratio of 1.49 and 100 liquidations over 18 hours split between $12,614 in longs and $604,883 in shorts. Ethereum showed negative 0.0039 percent per 8 hours (negative 4.3 percent annualized) with a 1.91 long-short ratio. Solana stood apart with positive 0.0073 percent per 8 hours (positive 8.0 percent annualized) and a 2.41 long-short ratio, with short liquidations of $2.16 million against longs of $53,007 over 22 hours. Stablecoin supply grew 0.67 percent over 30 days to $311 billion, providing $129.9 million in fresh buying power visible on the day.

Bitcoin difficulty is set to increase 3.7 percent at the next retarget, occurring at block 872 from the checkpoint. Outside the majors, altcoin movers showed STRK up 43.56 percent on the day and TIA up 25.42 percent, while KAIA fell 8.01 percent and ATOM dropped 5.75 percent.
